clips.text_zh: 又嚟同我講咩鐵律⋯⋯200SMA突破就算新牛？4年週期又話58K已經見底？即係個bear market得6個月？兩條rule根本唔夾，總有一條會失效。biz啲人又係咁，輸錢都唔肯認。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: AN UNBREAKABLE RULE OF CRYPTO HAS JUST BROKEN. Rule 1: breaking out from the 1D 200sma after a bear market starts the next bull run. Rule 2: the 4 year cycle. If this is the next bullrun, the bottom was 58k two months ago. That means the bear market was only 6 months long, when it was supposed to be about 12. These rules are incompatible at such an early month, so one of them is failing right now.
clips.source_hint: Biz thread about two crypto 'unbreakable rules' conflicting
clips.text_en_b2: Another supposedly ironclad rule of crypto just got shattered, and frankly, neither holds up. Rule one claims that breaking out from the 1D 200SMA after a bear market kickstarts the next bull run. Rule two insists on the sacred four-year cycle. If we genuinely entered a new bull market, the bottom was roughly 58K about two months back, which would imply the bear market lasted a mere six months rather than the expected twelve. At such an early stage, these two frameworks are fundamentally incompatible, meaning one of them is failing as we speak.
clips.text_en_c1: Another supposedly ironclad tenet of crypto markets has just been invalidated, and hardly anyone on the board is willing to confront it. The first rule holds that breaking above the 200 SMA on the daily chart after a bear market ushers in the subsequent bull run. The second asserts a strict four-year cycle. Taken together, however, the implications are mutually exclusive. If a new bull market has indeed commenced, the cycle bottomed at roughly 58K some two months ago, which would mean the preceding bear market lasted barely six months rather than the anticipated twelve. Both axioms cannot simultaneously hold at such an embryonic stage; one is necessarily failing.
clips.text_en_c2: Yet another invocation of crypto's so-called ironclad doctrines — as if either were remotely sacrosanct. The 200-day SMA breakout, we are solemnly assured, heralds the commencement of a fresh bull cycle. The quadrennial thesis, meanwhile, dictates that any meaningful bottom ought to have materialised around 58k a mere two months back, which would imply that the bear market limped along for only half its customary duration — roughly six months against an anticipated twelve. These two tenets are not merely in tension; they are mutually incompatible at so embryonic a juncture, and one of them is demonstrably failing even as we speak. The biz board, predictably, would rather lose money than concede the point. 🙄

clips.text_zh: USD要死又係新narrative？個post寫得好清楚，以往bullrun嗰啲liquidity已經無晒。BTC ETH可能仲有1-2x，其他細幣想moon？等下世啦。又係假pump，睇咗咁多年都未學精⋯⋯🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Is the USD 'dying' supposed to be the new narrative for why crypto is pumping? Why do I get the feeling this is just another one of those fake pumps we have been through many times before. BTC and ETH might be the only things that see a 1-2x, but there isn't enough liquidity for everything else to moon like we used to see in previous bullruns. Posted on /biz/ tonight.
clips.source_hint: Biz post questioning the USD dying pump narrative
clips.text_en_b2: So the USD allegedly 'dying' is meant to be the fresh narrative driving crypto higher? I cannot shake the suspicion that this is yet another one of those manufactured pumps we have witnessed countless times before. BTC and ETH might still squeeze out a modest 1-2x, although there simply is not enough liquidity left for altcoins to genuinely moon the way they did in previous bull cycles. After years of watching these setups fizzle out, you would think people would learn by now. Posted on /biz/ tonight.
clips.text_en_c1: Yet another thread proclaiming that the dollar is dying, which, if past experience is any guide, will probably be wheeled out to rationalise the latest rally. The accompanying post argues that the liquidity which propelled previous bull runs has effectively evaporated from the broader market. Bitcoin and Ethereum might conceivably still eke out a one-to-two-times move, but for smaller altcoins to moon in any meaningful sense seems increasingly implausible. I have witnessed this exact pattern repeat itself on multiple occasions, and each time the narrative has eventually collapsed under the weight of its own assumptions. Tonight's /biz/ discussion offers little to dispel that scepticism.
clips.text_en_c2: So the death of the US dollar is now the rallying cry for crypto's latest ascent? Forgive my scepticism, but there is a faintly déjà-vu quality to proceedings — the same theatrical pumps we have endured, what, half a dozen times by now? Liquidity, that elusive commodity which once greased the gears of every altcoin's parabolic fantasy, has effectively evaporated from the order books. Bitcoin and Ether might conceivably scrape out a modest 1–2x, given sufficient macro tailwind, but the broader alt universe is starved of the capital that once carried obscure tokens to astronomical valuations. If you are still waiting for a small-cap moon, I should temper expectations accordingly — perhaps in the next lifetime, perhaps never. 🧐

clips.text_zh: 睇完好嬲。8輪interview，recruiter一個月後先問啲resume已經有嘅嘢。Leetcode easy、medium，仲要寫test。我考HKIE都未搞惦，呢啲CS佬先係真正受苦。wtf。btw我都係想返US⋯⋯
clips.text_en_b1: How is this legal? Apply to faang. 8 rounds of interviews to get one job. Submit my resume. Recruiter reaches out a month later with a questionnaire asking the same stuff on my resume. Sent to screening rounds. 45 minute technical screening with mid level engineer, leetcode easy plus writing tests. 1 hour technical screening 2 with senior engineer, leetcode medium plus soft questions.
clips.source_hint: G thread about the absurd faang interview gauntlet
clips.text_en_b2: How on earth is this process even remotely legal? I applied to a FAANG company and endured eight gruelling interview rounds just to land a single offer. I submitted my resume, and a recruiter eventually followed up a full month later with a questionnaire that essentially recycled information already printed on my CV. That got me a forty-five minute technical screening with a mid-level engineer featuring Leetcode easy problems and writing tests, followed by a one-hour second screening with a senior engineer covering Leetcode medium questions alongside soft behavioural prompts.
clips.text_en_c1: Having recently endured the entire FAANG gauntlet myself, I can attest that the process is, in practical terms, nothing short of absurd. Following the submission of my resume, a recruiter contacted me roughly a month later requesting information that was plainly evident on the original document. Subsequent screening rounds comprised a forty-five-minute technical interview with a mid-level engineer, featuring a Leetcode easy problem alongside the writing of unit tests, followed by a one-hour session with a senior engineer involving a Leetcode medium and assorted behavioural questions. Eight rounds, in aggregate, to obtain a single offer.
clips.text_en_c2: One can scarcely credit that such an arrangement passes for legitimate. Consider the ordinary indignity: a candidate submits a CV, waits a full calendar month, and is then contacted by a recruiter who, with admirable diligence, proceeds to interrogate them about precisely the items already enumerated on the résumé. After that preliminary farce, one is shuttled through a forty-five-minute technical screening with a mid-level engineer, who cheerfully requests Leetcode easy alongside handwritten unit tests — an exercise in redundancy bordering on the surreal. A second round, an hour long with a senior engineer, demands Leetcode medium peppered with insipid soft-skill interrogations. Eight rounds, in aggregate, for a single position. Meanwhile, I have yet to finalise my own professional certification, and I daresay these computer scientists are bearing the genuine brunt of suffering. Meanwhile, I am still trying to relocate to the US. 😤

The thread itself, posted on /pol/ with the usual 4chan flavour, is frustratingly light on concrete numbers. clips.text_en_c1: An intriguing thread surfaced on /pol/ today announcing that Japan intends to raise its visa fees effective July 2026, with the notable caveat that Indian nationals will remain exempt from the increase. Whilst the post itself is somewhat light on granular financial detail, the broader implication is straightforward: travellers of every other nationality will henceforth incur a higher charge, whereas Indian applicants will continue to pay the existing rate. The usual 4chan commentary accompanies the article, though the precise magnitude of the hike has yet to be clarified in subsequent replies.
clips.text_en_c2: A rather intriguing piece of news from /pol/, delivered with the customary 4chan panache. From July the first, 2026, Japan intends to raise its visa fees across the board — a routine adjustment, one might assume, except that Indian nationals have been conspicuously carved out of the increment and will continue to pay the existing rate. The headline, naturally, generates more heat than light; the thread itself is frustratingly reticent about the precise quantum of the increase, preferring bombast to arithmetic. What one can confidently extract is the asymmetry itself: Indian travellers retain the old fee while everyone else, presumably the Chinese, the Southeast Asians, and assorted Westerners, shall henceforth be lighter in the pocket. I have not yet set foot in Japan — the licence comes first — but I shall be following developments with interest. lol.

clips.text_zh: Duskbloods beta真係笑死人。20fps、900p、online廢到30分鐘先match到人，From都話要做emergency PS5 port。等等，咁我部Switch食雞？lol。我仲以為任天堂會carry，點知⋯⋯🙏
clips.text_en_b1: The Duskbloods beta was a MASSIVE flop. It barely runs at 20 fps. Docked is 900p. The gameplay loop is boring. Nintendo's online is shitty. Matchmaking takes 30 minutes to find players because no one has a Switch. The few people playing it are hating it. Apparently From is already doing an emergency ps5 port to save the game.
clips.source_hint: V thread roasting the Duskbloods Switch beta
clips.text_en_b2: The Duskbloods beta turned out to be an absolute disaster, and barely a soul is surprised. Performance was borderline unplayable, hovering around 20fps with a docked resolution stuck at a miserable 900p. The gameplay loop itself felt painfully shallow, while Nintendo's online infrastructure made matchmaking an exercise in frustration, often forcing players to wait roughly thirty minutes just to find opponents, largely because hardly anyone owns a Switch. The handful of people who stuck with it openly despised the experience, and FromSoftware is reportedly scrambling to develop an emergency PS5 port in a desperate bid to salvage the project.
clips.text_en_c1: The closed beta for Duskbloods has, by any reasonable measure, been an unmitigated disaster. Performance hovers around a dismal twenty frames per second, with docked output capped at a mere 900p, whilst matchmaking routinely demands upwards of thirty minutes to assemble a viable lobby owing to the Switch's notoriously sparse online population. Those few players who have managed to connect describe the experience in uniformly scathing terms. Reports now suggest that FromSoftware is preparing an emergency PS5 port in a desperate attempt to salvage the title, which raises the inevitable question of whether the Switch hardware was ever a viable target.
clips.text_en_c2: The Duskbloods beta has, by any reasonable measure, been an unmitigated embarrassment. Performance craters to a laughable twenty frames per second, docked resolution limps along at a sub-HD nine hundred pixels, and the online component — that perpetual Achilles' heel of Nintendo's ecosystem — is so dysfunctional that matchmaking occasionally requires the better part of half an hour to assemble a single session. The few hardy souls who persist are, by all accounts, vocally appalled. FromSoftware, perhaps sensing the wreckage, is reportedly scrambling an emergency PS5 port in a belated effort to salvage the title. Whether the Switch hardware was ever genuinely capable of hosting such an undertaking remains, charitably, an open question — though I confess I had rather anticipated Nintendo's stewardship would prove more competent than this. 🙏

clips.text_en_b1: Why do office workers get fat? I got my first big boy job in an office after graduating college in accounting. The vast majority of people in my office are overweight and out of shape. The rest is skinny fat. I am the only guy who is lean and muscular. During college I had time to work out 5x a week, gym 3x and running 2x. I am kinda scared that I will end up like them.
clips.source_hint: Fit thread about office workers gaining weight
clips.text_en_b2: Why do office workers inevitably end up overweight? I landed my first proper accounting job straight out of college, and the pattern became glaringly obvious within weeks. The vast majority of my colleagues are visibly overweight and clearly out of shape, while the remainder fall into the skinny-fat category. I happen to be the only lean, muscular guy on the team, which is hardly surprising given that during university I could comfortably hit the gym three times a week and run twice. Honestly, I am genuinely terrified of eventually turning into them.
clips.text_en_c1: Upon returning to the office following the completion of a recent field survey, I was struck by an observation that the original poster articulated with considerable accuracy. The overwhelming majority of my colleagues have visibly put on weight, whilst the remainder exhibit that peculiarly unflattering combination of leanness paired with negligible muscle mass. During my university years, I maintained a rigorous regimen of five weekly sessions, comprising three resistance-training workouts and two cardiovascular sessions. The sedentary nature of professional life, however, now poses a genuine threat to that discipline, and I confess to harbouring growing concern about eventually conforming to the prevailing office physique.
clips.text_en_c2: The post articulates something uncomfortably germane. Having recently completed my surveying qualification and settled into a proper desk-bound role, I find the office landscape frankly dismaying: the overwhelming majority of my colleagues are visibly overweight and frankly out of shape, while the remainder present that insidious hybrid — skinny-fat, technically slim yet entirely devoid of musculature. I appear to be the sole specimen who is both lean and properly built, a state I attribute to the relative abundance of hours that university once afforded — gym thrice weekly, running twice, the sort of routine a nine-to-five quietly erodes. The prospect of gradually resembling them, of metabolically surrendering to the relentless tide of sedentary minutes and opportunistic snacking, genuinely unsettles me. My friend messaged today about the gym; I declined, citing exam revision. I must remember to keep lifting, lest I become a cautionary tale. 🧐

clips.text_en_c1: A thread on /v/ has prompted considerable discussion by posing a question that resonates strongly with anyone weary of the prevailing dodge-roll paradigm in contemporary action RPGs. The original poster explicitly rejects the so-called rollslop formula, in which combat devolves into an endless procession of evasive rolls and desperate dodges, and instead demands encounters possessing genuine heft, meaningful impact, and adversaries capable of punishing reckless play. No specific title has yet been endorsed, though the ensuing replies thread already runs to considerable length, suggesting that the community at large shares this mounting frustration with the genre's current direction.
clips.text_en_c2: A kindred spirit on /v/ has posed a question that resonates with mounting urgency: amid the contemporary proliferation of rollslop combat — that tiresome choreography of perpetual dodge-rolling, invincibility frames, and weightless exchanges — which action RPG actually delivers combat possessed of genuine heft, palpable impact, and adversaries who credibly threaten the player in return? The inquiry is refreshingly specific; no candidate title is volunteered, only the desiderata and an extensive replies thread awaiting substance. One might propose the usual suspects — the soulslike pantheon, the disciplined encounter design of Nioh, the meticulous parry-and-punish architecture of certain FromSoftware interlopers — though I shall refrain from pontificating until my own examinations are behind me. Consider this a bookmark, pending further investigation. lol. 🙏
